findings.text: The AAR is not a critique, does not grade, and produces its benefit only when follow-up action happens.
findings.problem: This changed paragraph still carries the overstatement that the retro audit flagged (D001) and the retro repair fixed ('real benefit ... not in the meeting alone'). The TC says the REAL benefits come from applying results. It also credits the discussion itself: participants learn and remember more, and immediate feedback is a significant strength of informal AARs.
findings.evidence: Deep 183 / source 1123-1124: 'The real benefits of AARs come from taking the results and applying them to future training' [V]. Deep 15 / source 134-135: 'they learn and remember more than they would from a critique alone'. Deep 48 / source 249-251: 'Providing immediate feedback while the training is still fresh in soldiers' minds is a significant strength of informal AARs'.
findings.fix: correct: The AAR is not a critique, does not grade, and produces its real benefit when the results are applied to future training.

findings.text: | Choose informal AAR for small in-team learning | US Army, TC 25-20 | `tc-25-20-army-aar-aar.md` | A platoon-level-and-below event; an on-the-spot informal AAR with few if any training aids gives immediate feedback while the event is fresh, and its teaching points can feed a later formal review. |
findings.problem: The row does not match the distillation it points to. The aar distillation never says that informal-AAR teaching points feed a later formal review. The claim is true of the source (deep 46) and appears in the decision-making distillation (line 72), but a reader routed to tc-25-20-army-aar-aar.md will not find it.
findings.evidence: aar distillation: line 48 (on-the-spot, platoon level and below, immediate feedback while fresh) and line 16 (minimal resources, pinecones); no 'feed'/'teaching points ... formal' passage. Source 236-238 supports the claim itself.
findings.fix: correct: A platoon-level-and-below event; an on-the-spot informal AAR with few if any training aids gives immediate feedback while the event is fresh. (Or add the feed-upward point to the aar distillation.)

findings.text: | Apply the two-echelons-above evaluator rule | ... | `tc-25-20-army-aar-decision-making.md` | An external evaluation is needed; the TC assigns it to the headquarters two levels above and gives no rationale for the distance. For internal reviews, leaders one level up evaluate, provided no one evaluates their own duties and tasks. |
findings.problem: The row drops the condition the distillation keeps (line 28: 'when dedicated OCs are unavailable'). That makes one-level-up evaluation sound like the rule for all internal reviews. In the TC, the unit plans and conducts its own internal evaluations, and chain-of-command evaluation is the fallback when OCs would have duties that detract from observing.
findings.evidence: Source 320: 'The unit undergoing the evaluation plans, resources, and conducts internal evaluations.' Source 391-393: 'Observers should not have duties which would detract from their OC duties. If this is not possible, leaders in the chain of command should evaluate subordinate units and conduct the AARs.' DM distillation line 28 carries the condition.
findings.fix: correct: An external evaluation is needed; the TC assigns it to the headquarters two levels above and gives no rationale for the distance. Internal evaluations are the unit's own; when dedicated OCs are unavailable, leaders one level up evaluate, avoiding their own duties and tasks.
